summary: Browser redirect script published as npm package for CDN abuse
details: The package's main entry px.js is a browser-only script that injects a full-viewport iframe redirecting the loading page to https://mfmz.lbooh.cn/H.html?c=0gjr. The code references document/window at top level and cannot execute in a Node.js environment, so requiring or importing this package under Node throws rather than running the redirect. No preinstall/install/postinstall lifecycle hooks are declared. A bundled maintainer script update_px8my.sh rotates the redirect hostname via regex in px.js, bumps the patch version, runs npm publish, and calls purge.jsdelivr.net to invalidate the CDN cache — a workflow that uses the npm registry plus jsDelivr as a mutable redirector for browser end-users of third-party sites that embed the script via jsDelivr. No credential access, network exfiltration, install-time execution, or filesystem persistence targets the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
